title: George Williams brass band versus Eureka and Young Tuxedo
summary: Wood heard the George Williams band a few times, thought it worse than Eureka and Young Tuxedo, which Bill Russell disagreed with.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: No. I don't think you do. Do you remember the George Williams brass band?

Well, I heard them on the streets a couple of times. They were not there a lot. And whenever they were there, I remember, you know, that people would say, oh, you know, like Irvin Helfer would say, gee, we really want to make sure we go and hear them. That's all. But other than the fact that I know they were there, and in fact they were this set of pictures that I gave you, there's one I have, they were in that, they were in that parade. But I don't have any real recollection of any sort of distinctive sound or playing that they were doing.
You don't remember that they were better or worse than the Eureka?
Oh, I think they were worse than the Eureka and the Young Tuxedo, which were the two that were really, I thought, the best two bands that we heard.
Well, most, so do I, but Bill Russell, for example, liked the George Williams battle.
Of course, they had a clarinet in there, and he liked that clarinet player, I guess.
